lessons: Football: veto every positive Asian handicap unless ai_chance clears break-even by at least 3 points AND 'why' names a concrete fact. The old 'back positive cushions' lesson is retired. Record: 6/11 won in the newest 120, about -32%. Hypothesis (n=11), but still the clearest loser.

Football: 'Team A or Team B' is a 12 pick, loses on a draw, and has no draw protection; never write '1X/X2' for it. Lower is the default verdict for a 12 pick: lowered 12 picks won 15/17, backed ones 18/24 (5/8 at prices of 1.30 or longer).
Football: veto 'Win to Nil - no' at 1.25 or shorter unless a confirmed fact points to the opponent scoring. It won 4/8 (about -39%) and was never vetoed. Hypothesis (n=8).

Football: missing squad-value % on its own is not a reason to back, lower or veto. Name the player and their role. Backs resting on 20%+ missing won 11/15 (73%, below ~78% break-even), and key_absences picks ran 8-12 points below the market rate.

Football: veto only on a named, checkable fact (confirmed starter out, confirmed rotation) and state it in 'why'. 'LOSING record' is never the reason. Vetoed picks won 106/136, level with backs at 77/102.

Football: for Over 1.5 at 1.20-1.31, 'lower' is the default; never veto it on record alone. It won 22/26, about break-even at +4%. For team-goal picks with a WINNING family record, keep the verdict at back: 9/10. Hypothesis (n=10).

Many 'why' fields lean on inputs the study does not grade: missing squad-value %, 'tactical matchup', pick_matchup_chance, 'paper study'. These need to become graded fact fields before they can be trusted.
